```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.
-->
```{steps: assembly}

# 1. Change directory to flye and setup a symbolic link to bbd read data

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/flye
ln -s /pvol/data/metagenome_assembly/bbd_0.1.fastq.gz

# 2. Run new shell script called run_flye_bbd.sh using a slurm script and save inside flye directory (separate text file)
# 3. Submit job (this could take several hours so starting it early is always ideal)

```{bash}
sbatch run_flye_bbd.sh

# 4. Check to see if job has been completed yet before moving on to <binning>

```{bash}
sacct -j XXX --format=JobID,State,MaxRSS,Elapsed

```
Assembly of the BBD nanopore reads with Flye. Commands for this step were run in `flye/`.
